turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. Sit yourself down. What's the problem?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): My big toe, doctor. Absolute agony since last night. I barely slept.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right or left?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Um, well, actually, yes, the right one.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is it swollen?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Really swollen. Can't get my trainer on. I don't know, doctor, it looks huge.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): And red?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not red. Just big and sore.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Can you walk?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Not a hope. I'm hopping. The duvet was enough to set it off.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I had a few pints Saturday, with the lads. I don't know if that's relevant.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever. Hot or shivery. Yes or no.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No temperature. Sorry, I thought you meant drink.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any injury to it?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. I don't think so.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did it start?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Last night. Fine at bedtime, woke about two, throbbing.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Score out of ten?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Nine. Goes to ten if I stand on it.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ever had this before?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Same thing about a year back. Might've been eighteen months. I don't know, doctor. Same toe, I think.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): What treatment?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Allopurinol, after it settled. I stopped it in March.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Why stop?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I felt fine. Didn't see the point carrying on.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you remember the dose?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No idea. It was once a day, that's all.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any other tablets now?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): The water tablet for my blood pressure. I can never pronounce it.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bendroflumethiazide?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): That's the one. Two and a half milligrams, I think, every morning.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many years?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Five-ish? Maybe longer. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Drink in the week or just weekends?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Weekends. Beer, four pints Saturday, sometimes five. Not every week, though.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never have.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any drug allergies?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None at all.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Socks and shoes off. Let me see the toe.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Hang on. This trainer is not cooperating.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hot, red and swollen over the right big toe joint. You can't bend it.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Red? Oh. Well, actually, looking at it, yes, it is red and shiny. I was wrong just now. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tender if I touch it?
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Very tender. Please don't. Even the sheet was agony.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Other joints? Ankles or knees?
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, the chair. I kicked the chair leg last night, coming back from the loo. Completely forgot. Does that count as an injury?
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm asking about other joints. Yes or no.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just this toe. But it was this toe I caught on the chair. I don't know if that kicked it all off.

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Most likely gout. I can't rule out a sprain from that knock, but it looks like gout. I'll start naproxen, five hundred milligrams twice a day with food for five days, plus a blood test for uric acid.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Naproxen? Is that like ibuprofen? Ibuprofen wrecked my stomach. I stopped it in March.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Were you taking ibuprofen regularly?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Four hundred milligrams, when the knee played up. Stopped in March. Stomach's been alright since.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): An ulcer, or heartburn?
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Heartburn. No ulcer. Nobody ever put a camera down. I don't know, doctor.

[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, scrap the naproxen. Same sort of drug, it'll stir your stomach again. Colchicine by mouth, five hundred micrograms twice a day for three days. Stop if you get diarrhoea.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): I've never had colchicine. Is it safe with the water tablet?
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep the bendroflumethiazide. Don't start the allopurinol again during this flare. We'll do the serum uric acid today, and kidney bloods, because of that water tablet.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): OK. I don't know, doctor. I work at a desk, accounts, so at least I'm sitting. The wife insisted I come.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cut the beer this weekend. Foot up, ice if you can tolerate it, nothing tight on the toe.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Will it be sorted for next week? I've got month-end at work.
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): See me in a week. If you're vomiting, or the redness is racing up the foot before then, get seen the same day.

spec.situation: Man with a very painful swollen big toe since last night; drinks beer at weekends, takes a water tablet; had the same 'a year back'; says no injury then recalls kicking a chair; colchicine or NSAID plan; blood uric acid test.
features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

omissions.text: Initial patient denial of redness was corrected after examination; there was disagreement/uncertainty about whether the toe was red before the doctor observed it was red and shiny.
The patient could barely walk / was hopping because of the toe pain.
Pain was triggered even by the duvet/bed sheet touching the toe.
No injury was initially reported, but later the patient remembered kicking the affected toe on a chair leg the previous night; this history changed during the consultation.
The previous similar episode was in the same toe, though the patient was unsure.
Allopurinol had been started after the previous episode settled, and the patient stopped it because he felt fine and did not see the point of continuing.
Duration of current bendroflumethiazide use was about 5 years or longer.
Doctor originally planned naproxen 500 mg twice a day with food for 5 days, then withdrew that plan because of the patient's prior ibuprofen-related stomach upset/heartburn.
The patient reported ibuprofen 'wrecked my stomach'; the adverse effect was heartburn rather than ulcer.
The patient asked whether colchicine was safe with the water tablet.
Red-flag advice was to get seen the same day if vomiting occurs or if redness is spreading/racing up the foot before the 1-week review.
